title: Randomized Comparison of Percutaneous Repair and Surgery for Mitral Regurgitation: 5-Year Results of EVEREST II.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, patients with grade 3+ or 4+ MR assigned 2:1 to percutaneous repair or surgery (178:80).
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract describes an unequal 2:1 allocation and an as-treated analysis; the abstract gives no confidence intervals.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year results of the randomised comparison of percutaneous edge-to-edge mitral repair with surgery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years, the rate of the composite endpoint of freedom from death, surgery, or 3+ or 4+ MR in the as-treated population was 44.2% versus 64.3% in the percutaneous repair and surgical groups, respectively (p = 0.01). Five-year mortality rates were 20.8% and 26.8% (p = 0.4) for percutaneous repair and surgery, respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It gives durability data for transcatheter mitral repair against surgery and shows that most additional surgery occurred early.

title: Initial Experience With Commercial Transcatheter Mitral Valve Repair in the United States.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: National registry; 564 patients, median age 83 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm registry without a comparator or core-laboratory adjudication, and with short follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Early US commercial experience with transcatheter mitral repair in prohibitive-risk primary MR from the TVT Registry.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In-hospital mortality was 2.3%; 30-day mortality was 5.8%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives contemporary real-world safety and efficacy benchmarks for transcatheter mitral repair.

title: Two-Year Outcomes of Surgical Treatment of Moderate Ischemic Mitral Regurgitation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 301 patients assigned to CABG alone or the combined procedure.
appraisal.main_limitation: Primary end point was a remodelling measure rather than a clinical event, and the trial was not powered for survival.
appraisal.one_line: Two-year outcomes of CABG alone versus CABG plus mitral repair for moderate ischaemic mitral regurgitation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The rate of death was 10.6% in the CABG-alone group and 10.0% in the combined-procedure group (hazard ratio in the combined-procedure group, 0.90; 95% confidence interval, 0.45 to 1.83; P=0.78). The 2-year rate of moderate or severe residual mitral regurgitation was higher in the CABG-alone group than in the combined-procedure group (32.3% vs. 11.2%, P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It informs whether to treat moderate ischaemic MR at the time of revascularisation.

title: Papillary Muscle Approximation Versus Restrictive Annuloplasty Alone for Severe Ischemic Mitral Regurgitation.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, ninety-six patients with severe ischemic MR.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample, a remodelling primary endpoint, and no difference in mortality.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of papillary muscle approximation added to restrictive annuloplasty for severe ischaemic MR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years, mean LVEDD was 56.5 ± 5.7 mm with PMA versus 60.6 ± 4.6 mm with RA (mean change from baseline -5.8 ± 4.1 mm and -0.2 ± 2.3 mm, respectively; p < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It tests a subvalvular repair technique for ischaemic MR, a setting where transcatheter options are also evolving.

title: 2016 Annual Report of The Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: National registry annual report; 54,782 patients with transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
appraisal.main_limitation: Descriptive report without adjustment for case-mix change or causal inference.
appraisal.one_line: Annual TVT Registry report describing US transcatheter aortic and mitral valve procedure trends and outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Observed in-hospital mortality decreased from 5.7% to 2.9%, and 1-year mortality decreased from 25.8% to 21.6%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Documents practice trends including a rise in pacemaker insertion.

title: Outcome after percutaneous edge-to-edge mitral repair for functional and degenerative mitral regurgitation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: Heart (British Cardiac Society)

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of nine studies (n=2615), registered with PROSPERO.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, mostly single-arm data with aetiology-level comparisons that are confounded.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis comparing outcomes of MitraClip edge-to-edge repair for functional and degenerative mitral regurgitation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, there were not significant differences among groups in terms of patients with MR grade≤2 (RR 1.12; 95% CI: 0.86 to 1.47; p=0.40), while there was a significantly lower rate of mitral valve re-intervention in patients with functional MR (RR 0.60; 95% CI: 0.38 to 0.97; p=0.04).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Summarises mid-term TEER outcomes by aetiology before the randomised trials in functional MR reported.

title: 2017 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway on the Management of Mitral Regurgitation: A Report of the American College of Cardiology Task Force on Expert Consensus Decision Pathways.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Expert consensus decision pathway; no sample size applies.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus guidance with limited randomised evidence for transcatheter options at the time of writing.
appraisal.one_line: ACC expert consensus decision pathway on the management of mitral regurgitation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It sets out a structured approach to mechanism, severity and timing of intervention in mitral regurgitation by a heart team.

title: Percutaneous Repair or Medical Treatment for Secondary Mitral Regurgitation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; severe secondary mitral regurgitation; intervention group 83 of 152 patients with the primary outcome and control group 78 of 152 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design; patient selection and medical therapy optimisation differ from the contemporaneous US trial.
appraisal.one_line: Open-label trial found no benefit of percutaneous mitral repair over medical therapy in severe secondary mitral regurgitation, contrasting with COAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12 months, the rate of the primary outcome was 54.6% (83 of 152 patients) in the intervention group and 51.3% (78 of 152 patients) in the control group (odds ratio, 1.16; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 1.84; P=0.53).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Together with discordant results from another trial it defines the central open question for TEER in secondary MR.

title: Transcatheter Mitral-Valve Repair in Patients with Heart Failure.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial at 78 sites in the United States and Canada; 614 patients enrolled (302 device, 312 control).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, with highly selected patients on maximal medical therapy; sharply contrasts with other trial.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial showing transcatheter mitral repair plus medical therapy reduced heart failure hospitalisation and mortality in secondary MR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The annualized rate of all hospitalizations for heart failure within 24 months was 35.8% per patient-year in the device group as compared with 67.9% per patient-year in the control group (hazard ratio, 0.53; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.40 to 0.70; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides the first randomised mortality benefit for TEER in heart failure and changes practice and guidelines.

title: Outcomes of transcatheter mitral valve replacement for degenerated bioprostheses, failed annuloplasty rings, and mitral annular calcification.
journal: European heart journal

appraisal.design_and_n: TMVR multicentre registry of 521 patients (322 with ViV, 141 with ViR, 58 with ViMAC).
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised registry without a surgical comparator.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre registry of transcatheter mitral valve-in-valve, valve-in-ring and valve-in-MAC procedures showing worse outcomes in the latter two.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality was higher after ViMAC compared with ViR and ViV at 30 days (34.5% vs. 9.9% vs. 6.2%; log-rank P < 0.001) and 1 year (62.8% vs. 30.6% vs. 14.0%; log-rank P < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs patient selection for transcatheter mitral replacement in failed repairs and calcified annuli.

title: Health Status After Transcatheter Mitral-Valve Repair in Heart Failure and Secondary Mitral Regurgitation: COAPT Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial secondary analysis (COAPT); TMVr (n = 302) versus standard care (n = 312).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with patient-reported outcomes may inflate the treatment effect.
appraisal.one_line: COAPT health status analysis shows transcatheter mitral repair improved KCCQ scores and the proportion alive with substantial improvement versus standard care at 24 months.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 month the mean between-group difference in KCCQ-OS was 15.9 points (95% confidence interval [CI]: 12.3 to 19.5 points), and 12.8 points at 24 months (95% CI: 7.5 to 18.2 points). At 24 months, 36.4% of TMVr patients were alive with a moderately large (≥10-point) improvement versus 16.6% of standard care patients (p < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Complements the mortality and hospitalisation benefit of TEER in secondary mitral regurgitation with symptom data.

title: Transcatheter Versus Medical Treatment of Patients With Symptomatic Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry-based propensity-matched case-control study; 472 TTVI patients and 1,179 medically managed controls, 268 matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Matching on only three variables with retrospective controls, so residual confounding and selection are likely.
appraisal.one_line: TriValve propensity-matched registry comparison associated transcatheter tricuspid intervention with lower 1-year mortality and heart failure rehospitalisation than medical therapy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with control subjects, TTVI patients had lower 1-year mortality (23 ± 3% vs. 36 ± 3%; p = 0.001), rehospitalization (26 ± 3% vs. 47 ± 3%; p < 0.0001), and composite endpoint (32 ± 4% vs. 49 ± 3%; p = 0.0003).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives early comparative signal for T-TEER and TTVR where randomised evidence is lacking.

title: 2020 Focused Update of the 2017 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway on the Management of Mitral Regurgitation: A Report of the American College of Cardiology Solution Set Oversight Committee.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Expert consensus decision pathway; no sample size applicable.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus pathway rather than graded recommendations; abstract gives no quantitative content.
appraisal.one_line: Focused update of the ACC expert consensus pathway on mitral regurgitation management.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Updates the assessment and intervention pathway for MR in light of new secondary MR trial data.

title: Pulmonary Hypertension in Transcatheter Mitral Valve Repair for Secondary Mitral Regurgitation: The COAPT Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of the randomised COAPT trial; 528 patients with PASP data (184 with PASP of 50 mm Hg or more).
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc, 86 of 614 patients lacked PASP data.
appraisal.one_line: COAPT analysis: baseline pulmonary hypertension worsened prognosis but did not alter the benefit of transcatheter mitral repair in secondary MR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Death or HF hospitalisation at 2 years was 68.8% vs 49.1% with PASP of at least 50 vs below 50 mm Hg (adjusted HR 1.52; 95% CI 1.17 to 1.97). Benefit of TMVr was irrespective of baseline PASP (pinteraction = 0.45).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports offering TEER in secondary MR even with pulmonary hypertension.

title: 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease: Executive Summary: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
journal: Circulation

appraisal.design_and_n: Guideline executive summary; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Many recommendations rest on lower levels of evidence; the abstract gives no class or level detail.
appraisal.one_line: 2020 ACC/AHA valvular heart disease guideline executive summary, including timing and choice of surgical and catheter interventions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Primary US reference for TAVI, mitral and tricuspid intervention decisions, to compare with ESC guidance.

title: 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease: Executive Summary: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Guideline executive summary; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Same document as the Circulation publication; recommendation levels not given in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: 2020 ACC/AHA valvular heart disease guideline executive summary (JACC publication), covering diagnostic work-up and timing and choice of interventions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Primary US reference for valve intervention decisions; duplicate publication of the same guideline.

title: 3-Year Outcomes of Transcatheter Mitral Valve Repair in Patients With Heart Failure.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 614 patients with HF and moderate-to-severe or severe secondary MR; NCT01626079.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label; control crossover after 24 months limits the late comparison; mortality was a secondary endpoint.
appraisal.one_line: COAPT at 36 months: transcatheter mitral repair plus GDMT reduced heart failure hospitalisation and mortality versus GDMT alone in secondary MR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Annualised HFH rates per patient-year were 35.5% with TMVr and 68.8% with GDMT alone (HR 0.49; 95% CI 0.37 to 0.63; p < 0.001). Mortality was 42.8% vs 55.5% (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.52 to 0.85; p = 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Durable survival benefit supports TEER in carefully selected secondary MR, after conflicting earlier randomised trials.

title: The management of secondary mitral regurgitation in patients with heart failure: a joint position statement from the Heart Failure Association (HFA), European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging (EACVI), European Heart Rhythm Association (EHRA), and European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) of the ESC.
journal: European heart journal

appraisal.design_and_n: Position statement; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert position drawing on conflicting randomised trials.
appraisal.one_line: Joint HFA/EAPCI/EACVI/EHRA position statement on management of secondary mitral regurgitation, including transcatheter repair.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: European society positioning on TEER in secondary MR after conflicting trials.

title: Mitral Surgery After Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: Society of Thoracic Surgeons Database Analysis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: STS Adult Cardiac Surgery Database, 463 patients undergoing mitral surgery after TEER (524 identified before exclusions).
appraisal.main_limitation: Registry of surgical cases only, so TEER failures managed otherwise are not captured.
appraisal.one_line: STS database analysis showed mitral repair was seldom achieved after failed TEER and operative mortality was high at low-volume centres.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In patients undergoing isolated mitral surgery, the median STS-predicted mortality was 6.5% (IQR: 3.9% to 10.5%), the observed mortality was 10.2% (n = 23 of 225), and the ratio of observed to expected mortality was 1.2 (95% CI: 0.8 to 1.9).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs consent and patient selection for TEER in younger, lower-risk patients with degenerative disease.

title: Mechanical Complications of Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
journal: Circulation

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few high-quality studies guide practice, as the statement notes.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement on mechanical complications of acute MI, including papillary muscle rupture, ventricular septal defect and free wall rupture.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Reference position on a high-mortality complication group with considerable practice variation.

title: Burden, treatment use, and outcome of secondary mitral regurgitation across the spectrum of heart failure: observational cohort study.
journal: BMJ (Clinical research ed.)

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational cohort, 13 223 patients with sMR; severe sMR in 1317 patients (10%).
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-region observational data with echocardiographic grading and no treatment effect estimate.
appraisal.one_line: Large Viennese cohort showed secondary MR is common, associated with excess mortality across heart failure types and rarely treated.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In comparison with patients with heart failure and no/mild sMR, mortality increased stepwise with a hazard ratio of 1.29 (95% confidence interval 1.20 to 1.38, P<0.001) for moderate and 1.82 (1.64 to 2.02, P<0.001) for severe sMR.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies the untreated burden relevant to TEER eligibility.

title: Conservative, surgical, and percutaneous treatment for mitral regurgitation shortly after acute myocardial infarction.
journal: European heart journal

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective international registry, 471 patients in 21 centres; 205 underwent interventions (106 surgical, 99 percutaneous).
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective with selection and survivor bias in who received intervention.
appraisal.one_line: International registry associated mitral intervention after MI with lower mortality than conservative care, with percutaneous repair faring better than surgery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patients who underwent mitral valve intervention had lower in-hospital and 1-year mortality compared with those treated conservatively [11% vs. 27%, P < 0.01 and 16% vs. 35%, P < 0.01; adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 0.28, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.18-0.46, P < 0.01]. SMVR versus PMVR: adjusted HR 3.75, 95% CI 1.55-9.07, P < 0.01.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Guidelines are inconclusive on post-MI mitral regurgitation and the registry informs transcatheter options.

title: 2-Year Outcomes of Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement in Patients With Severe Symptomatic Mitral Regurgitation.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Expanded Clinical Study of the Tendyne Mitral Valve System (NCT02321514), first 100 patients, open-label nonrandomised.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm study in a selected high-risk population without a control group.
appraisal.one_line: Two-year outcomes of the Tendyne transapical TMVR study showed sustained MR elimination with substantial early mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 2 years, all-cause mortality was 39.0%; 17 (43.6%) of 39 deaths occurred during the first 90 days. At 2 years, 93.2% of surviving patients had no MR.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Intermediate-term evidence for a TMVR device in patients unsuitable for surgery.

title: Concomitant Tricuspid Repair in Patients with Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 401 patients undergoing mitral-valve surgery for degenerative mitral regurgitation.
appraisal.main_limitation: The benefit was driven by progression of tricuspid regurgitation rather than clinical outcomes, and follow-up was 2 years.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial found that adding tricuspid annuloplasty to mitral surgery reduced a composite of tricuspid events at 2 years, with more pacemaker implantation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary event rate was 3.9% vs. 10.2% (relative risk, 0.37; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.16 to 0.86; P = 0.02). Permanent pacemaker implantation was 14.1% vs. 2.5% (rate ratio, 5.75; 95% CI, 2.27 to 14.60).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs timing of tricuspid intervention and the surgical comparator for transcatheter tricuspid and mitral therapies.

title: Outcomes Stratified by Adapted Inclusion Criteria After Mitral Edge-to-Edge Repair.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry analysis (EuroSMR) of 1,022 patients treated with M-TEER, stratified into COAPT-eligible (n = 353 [34.5%]) and COAPT-ineligible (n = 669 [65.5%]) groups.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective application of approximated trial criteria in a non-randomised registry without a medical therapy comparator.
appraisal.one_line: Retrospective application of COAPT and MITRA-FR style criteria to a European M-TEER registry for secondary MR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Adapted MITRA-FR criteria gave comparable outcomes regarding all-cause mortality (P = 0.19), whereas COAPT-eligible patients had lower mortality than COAPT-ineligible patients (P < 0.001). Right ventricular-to-pulmonary arterial coupling was an independent predictor (HR: 0.10; 95% CI: 0.02-0.57; P = 0.009).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It speaks to patient selection for M-TEER in secondary MR, where the two defining trials conflicted.

title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Mitral Valve Repair in Patients With Severe Mitral Regurgitation and Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry analysis; 3,797 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, with device success defined post hoc and subject to survivor and selection bias.
appraisal.one_line: STS/ACC TVT Registry analysis found device success of TEER in cardiogenic shock with mitral regurgitation was associated with lower 1-year mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year after TEER, device success was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (34.6% vs 55.5%; adjusted HR: 0.49; 95% CI: 0.41-0.59; P < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Hypothesis-generating data for TEER in shock (D4, D2), where no randomised trial exists.

title: Factors influencing post-surgical survival in degenerative mitral regurgitation.
journal: European heart journal

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 2276 patients undergoing mitral valve surgery across five centres; 278 patients (12.2%) died over median follow-up of 5.6 (3.6 to 8.7) years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry data from five centres with residual confounding possible; the abstract does not describe transcatheter alternatives.
appraisal.one_line: Registry cohort relating the number of secondary outcome determinants to survival after surgery for degenerative mitral regurgitation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Adjusted hazard ratios for post-operative all-cause mortality were 1.56 (95% CI: 1.11-2.20), 1.78 (95% CI: 1.23-2.58) and 2.58 (95% CI: 1.73-3.83) for one, two, and three or four secondary outcome determinants respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports earlier surgical referral thresholds and informs the choice between surgery and transcatheter repair in degenerative mitral regurgitation.

title: Five-Year Follow-up after Transcatheter Repair of Secondary Mitral Regurgitation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 614 patients, 302 assigned to the device group and 312 to the control group.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with crossover and attrition over five years.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year follow-up of transcatheter repair for secondary mitral regurgitation in heart failure.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality through 5 years was 57.3% in the device group and 67.2% in the control group (hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.89); hospitalization for heart failure hazard ratio was 0.53 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.41 to 0.68).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Confirms durable survival and heart failure benefit of mitral TEER in selected patients with secondary mitral regurgitation.

title: Transcatheter Mitral Valve Repair for Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation.
journal: JAMA

appraisal.design_and_n: Cohort study of 19 088 patients with degenerative MR in the STS/ACC Transcatheter Valve Therapies Registry, 2014 through 2022.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry without a surgical or medical comparator; procedural success is partly selected by anatomy.
appraisal.one_line: Registry cohort of transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for degenerative MR relating residual MR and mitral gradient to one-year outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MR success was achieved in 88.9% of patients. At 1 year, MR success compared with an unsuccessful procedure was associated with lower mortality (14.0% vs 26.7%; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.42-0.56; P < .001) and heart failure readmission (8.4% vs 16.9%; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.41-0.54; P < .001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large real-world dataset supporting procedural targets for TEER in degenerative MR.

title: Heart failure medical therapy prior to mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair: the STS/ACC Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry.
journal: European heart journal

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort in the STS/ACC Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry, 4199 patients across 449 sites, 2014 eligible for 1-year follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, with residual confounding and survivor selection among patients eligible for follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: US registry analysis of heart failure medical therapy before mitral TEER for functional MR and its association with one-year outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Triple therapy was prescribed for 19.2%, double therapy for 38.2%, single therapy for 36.0%, and 6.5% were on no GDMT. Compared with no/single therapy, triple therapy (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.73, 95% CI .55-.97) and double therapy (aHR 0.69, 95% CI .56-.86) were associated with lower risk of 1-year mortality or HFH.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows guideline-directed therapy is seldom optimised before TEER, a quality target in a population defined by COAPT-style selection.

title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair in 5,000 Patients With Secondary Mitral Regurgitation: COAPT Post-Approval Study.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Post-approval study of 5,000 patients, including COAPT-like (n = 991) and MITRA-FR-like (n = 917) subgroups.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison with trial arms from different eras and populations.
appraisal.one_line: Post-approval registry of transcatheter edge-to-edge repair in secondary mitral regurgitation, with comparison against COAPT and MITRA-FR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: One-year heart failure hospitalizations was 18.9% in COAPT-PAS and 19.7% in COAPT-like compared with 24.9% in COAPT-RCT, and 28.7% in COAPT-PAS-MITRA-FR-like compared with 47.4% in MITRA-FR-RCT.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Describes real-world use and outcomes of mitral TEER, including patients excluded from the trials.

title: Cardiac Reoperation or Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Patients With Failed Mitral Prostheses.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Medicare cohort of 4,293 patients (redo SMVR: 64%; TMVR: 36%); matched cohort n = 1,317 in each group.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, with residual confounding in a population where TMVR recipients were older and had more comorbidity.
appraisal.one_line: Medicare comparison of redo surgical mitral valve replacement and transcatheter mitral valve replacement for failed prostheses.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In the matched cohort, mid-term risk of MACE was similar (adjusted HR: 0.92; 95% CI: 0.80-1.04; P = 0.2). Landmark analysis showed a lower risk of MACE with TMVR in the first 6 months (adjusted HR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.63-0.88; P < 0.001) and a higher risk beyond 6 months (adjusted HR: 1.28; 95% CI: 1.04-1.58; P = 0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs a common decision for failed mitral bioprostheses with no randomised evidence.

title: Comparison of Direct Oral Anticoagulants vs Vitamin K Antagonists After Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective single-centre cohort of 156 patients undergoing transseptal TMVR with a SAPIEN family prosthesis, 2011 to 2023; 20.5% received DOACs and 79.5% VKAs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre, non-randomised with era-based allocation, short follow-up (median 4.7 months) and few DOAC patients.
appraisal.one_line: Single-centre prospective cohort comparing DOACs with vitamin K antagonists after transseptal TMVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome (bleeding) was observed in 50 (40%) patients in the VKA group and 3 (9%) patients in the DOAC group (adjusted HR: 0.21; 95% CI: 0.06-0.74; P = 0.02). No significant differences were found in terms of thrombotic events, major vascular complications, stroke, or death.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses an area with no established antithrombotic recommendation and supports a randomised comparison.

title: Artificial intelligence-derived risk score for mortality in secondary mitral regurgitation treated by transcatheter edge-to-edge repair: the EuroSMR risk score.
journal: European heart journal

appraisal.design_and_n: Derivation and validation in the EuroSMR cohort (4172 and 428 patients treated with M-TEER in the derivation and validation cohorts, respectively).
appraisal.main_limitation: Prognostic model without a randomised or comparative evaluation of treatment selection.
appraisal.one_line: Machine learning risk score (EuroSMR) predicting one-year outcomes after mitral TEER for secondary MR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The EuroSMR risk score allowed improved discrimination of surviving and non-surviving patients (hazard ratio 4.3, 95% confidence interval 3.7-5.0; P < .001). Prediction for 1-year mortality had an area under the curve of 0.789, 95% confidence interval 0.737-0.842.
appraisal.why_it_matters: May assist patient selection for TEER in secondary MR, though validation was in a smaller cohort.

title: Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair vs. isolated mitral surgery for severe mitral regurgitation: a French nationwide study.
journal: European heart journal

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationwide administrative database study, 57 030 patients, 2160 analysed in each arm after matching, 2012 to 2022.
appraisal.main_limitation: Administrative data with residual confounding and cause-of-death misclassification; no echocardiographic detail.
appraisal.one_line: French nationwide propensity-matched comparison of mitral TEER versus isolated mitral valve surgery for severe MR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 3-year follow-up, TEER was associated with a lower incidence of cardiovascular death (hazard ratio 0.685, 95% confidence interval 0.563-0.832; P = .0001), while non-cardiovascular death was more frequent (hazard ratio 1.562, 95% confidence interval 1.238-1.971; P = .0002). All-cause death did not differ (hazard ratio 0.967, 95% confidence interval 0.835-1.118; P = .65).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides large-scale comparative data in a decision lacking randomised evidence outside high-risk patients.

title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair in COAPT-Ineligible Patients With Functional Mitral Regurgitation.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 6,675 patients who underwent MTEER for FMR; 3,721 (55.7%) trial-eligible and 2,954 (44.3%) trial-ineligible.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry with no non-TEER comparator among ineligible patients, so benefit cannot be estimated.
appraisal.one_line: TVT Registry analysis of outcomes of mitral TEER in functional MR patients who would have been ineligible for COAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was a higher risk of 1-year death or HFH (HR: 1.73; 95% CI: 1.57-1.91; P < 0.001) in trial-ineligible patients. A clinically meaningful improvement in health status at 30 days was observed in 78.9% and 77.0% of patients in the trial-ineligible and trial-eligible groups, respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows nearly half of real-world patients lie outside the defining trial, a gap relevant to transportability work.

title: Contemporary Outcomes and Trends for the Transseptal Mitral Valve-in-Valve Procedure Using Balloon Expandable Transcatheter Valves in the United States.
journal: Circulation

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 4243 patients with a mean±SD STS score of 9.2±7.7 at 455 sites, 2015 to September 2022.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm registry without a surgical comparator.
appraisal.one_line: STS/ACC registry analysis of contemporary transseptal mitral valve-in-valve with balloon-expandable valves.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause in-hospital, 30-day, and 1-year mortality rates were 3.2%, 4.3%, and 13.4%, respectively. NYHA class I/II rose from 18% to 87% and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score from 38 to 78 at 1 year (P<0.0001 for both).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Contemporary benchmarks for transseptal MViV supporting its use in degenerated bioprostheses.

title: Transcatheter Valve Repair in Heart Failure with Moderate to Severe Mitral Regurgitation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: 505 patients randomised (250 device, 255 control) at 30 sites in nine countries.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label device trial funded by the manufacturer, in a population selected for moderate to severe regurgitation on medical therapy.
appraisal.one_line: RESHAPE-HF2 found transcatheter mitral repair plus medical therapy reduced heart failure hospitalisation or cardiovascular death and improved health status in functional mitral regurgitation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 24 months, the rate of first or recurrent hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death was 37.0 events per 100 patient-years in the device group and 58.9 events per 100 patient-years in the control group (rate ratio, 0.64; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.48 to 0.85; P = 0.002).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Resolves conflict between earlier TEER trials in functional MR and is likely to influence guideline recommendations.

title: Transcatheter Repair versus Mitral-Valve Surgery for Secondary Mitral Regurgitation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: 210 patients randomised in Germany to transcatheter edge-to-edge repair or surgical repair or replacement.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial with missing data for part of the cohort and a wide confidence interval around the difference.
appraisal.one_line: MATTERHORN found transcatheter edge-to-edge repair noninferior to mitral surgery for a one-year composite in secondary mitral regurgitation, with fewer early adverse events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Within 1 year, at least one of the components of the primary efficacy end point occurred in 16 of the 96 patients with available data (16.7%) in the intervention group and in 20 of the 89 with available data (22.5%) in the surgery group (estimated mean difference, -6 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -17 to 6; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First randomised comparison of TEER and surgery in secondary MR.

title: Tricuspid regurgitation and outcomes in mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair.
journal: European heart journal

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort in OCEAN-Mitral: 2103 (no TR), 201 (new-onset TR), 504 (normalized TR), and 858 (residual TR) patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with echocardiographic grouping defined after the procedure, so landmark and confounding issues remain.
appraisal.one_line: OCEAN-Mitral registry analysis linking post-procedural tricuspid regurgitation, rather than baseline TR, to outcomes after mitral TEER.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with no TR as a reference, hazard ratio 1.83 (95% confidence interval: 1.39-2.40) for new-onset TR, 1.45 (1.23-1.72) for residual TR, and 0.82 (0.65-1.04) for normalized TR for cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests post-procedural TR status, not baseline TR, is the relevant prognostic marker for concomitant tricuspid treatment decisions in mitral TEER.

title: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair vs medical therapy in atrial functional mitral regurgitation: a propensity score-based comparison from the OCEAN-Mitral and REVEAL-AFMR registries.
journal: European heart journal

appraisal.design_and_n: Two Japanese registries, 1081 patients with moderate or severe AFMR; 441 TEER and 640 medical therapy.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison across two registries with confidence intervals close to unity.
appraisal.one_line: Propensity-weighted comparison of mitral TEER with medical therapy in atrial functional MR from two registries.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TEER was associated with a lower incidence of the primary (hazard ratio [HR] 0.65, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.43-0.99, P = .044) and secondary endpoints (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.35-0.99, P = .044).
appraisal.why_it_matters: No randomised evidence exists for TEER in atrial functional MR, so this signal informs trial design and early practice.

title: Long-Term Outcomes of Early Surgery Versus Conventional Treatment for Asymptomatic Severe Mitral Regurgitation: A Propensity Analysis.
journal: Circulation

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective single-centre cohort of 1063 asymptomatic patients, 545 early surgery and 518 conventional treatment, 358 propensity-matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational and single-centre, with enrolment from 1996 to 2016 and treatment chosen by patient and physician.
appraisal.one_line: Propensity analysis of early surgery versus conventional treatment in asymptomatic severe degenerative MR over a median of 12 years.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 8 (1.5%) patients in the early surgery group and 54 (10.4%) in the conventional management group died from cardiovascular causes (hazard ratio, 0.17 [95% CI, 0.07-0.40]; P<0.001). All-cause mortality: hazard ratio, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.52-0.99]; P=0.046.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds long-term evidence on timing of intervention in asymptomatic severe MR, a decision with weak guideline support and ongoing trial interest.

title: Percutaneous transcatheter valve replacement in individuals with mitral regurgitation unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter edge-to-edge repair: a prospective, multicountry, single-arm trial.
journal: Lancet (London, England)

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre single-arm trial at 56 centres in six countries; 1171 patients screened, 299 treated.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm design against a performance goal with no randomised comparator, industry funded.
appraisal.one_line: Pivotal single-arm trial of the SAPIEN M3 transseptal TMVR in patients unsuitable for surgery or TEER.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint rate of 25·2% (95% CI 20·6-30·6) was significantly lower than the prespecified performance goal of 45% (p<0·0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First pivotal evidence for a transseptal TMVR system in patients with no current transcatheter or surgical option.

title: Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Severe Mitral Annular Calcification: Primary Outcomes From the SUMMIT-MAC Study.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective single-arm trial cohort of 103 high surgical risk patients with severe MAC, compared with a performance goal.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm design with a performance goal and no randomised comparator.
appraisal.one_line: SUMMIT-MAC reports 12-month primary outcomes of Tendyne transcatheter mitral replacement in severe mitral annular calcification.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Technical success was achieved in 94.2%, with a 30-day mortality of 6.8%. The primary endpoint was met: freedom from all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization was 60.4% at 12 months (performance goal: 43%; P = 0.0002).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides prospective trial evidence for a transcatheter option in a high-risk anatomy with limited alternatives.

title: Estimating the Effects of MTEER in U.S. Practice: A Transportability Analysis of the COAPT Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: COAPT trial data (614 patients) reweighted to 15,275 TVT Registry patients, of whom 7,289 were COAPT trial-eligible.
appraisal.main_limitation: Estimates depend on untestable assumptions such as conditional exchangeability and on measured covariates available in both sources.
appraisal.one_line: Transportability analysis estimates whether COAPT mitral TEER effects apply to US TVT registry patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MTEER in the trial-eligible population would result in 2-year absolute risk reductions of 17.0% for heart failure hospitalizations (95% CI: -28.7% to -5.7%) and 15.4% for all-cause death (95% CI: -26.6% to -5.2%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses the applicability of a landmark trial to routine practice where later trials gave mixed results.

title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society/Canadian Society of Cardiovascular Surgery/Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology Clinical Practice Update on Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Valve Intervention: Patient Evaluation and Management.
journal: The Canadian journal of cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical practice update from Canadian societies; the abstract gives no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not describe the evidence grading method.
appraisal.one_line: A Canadian clinical practice update on transcatheter mitral and tricuspid edge-to-edge repair and replacement.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It offers contemporary referral and patient-selection guidance across mitral and tricuspid transcatheter therapy.

title: Transseptal Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Mitral Annular Calcification: ENCIRCLE MAC Registry 1-Year Outcomes.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective, multicentre, single-arm registry; TMVR attempted in 100, valve implanted in 93.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm design without a comparator in a highly selected population.
appraisal.one_line: One-year outcomes of transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system in mitral annular calcification.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 33.6% (95% CI: 25.0%-44.1%), with 21.1% all-cause mortality and 19.4% HFH.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides the main prospective data for a transcatheter option in patients with mitral annular calcification who are unsuitable for surgery or repair.
